concerns.message: The plan doesn't say where each fighter's kit is stored. Today `DuelConfig` is `{ moveset }`. `movesetVersion` hashes only the moveset (version.ts:52), `stepDuel` and `restoreDuel` refuse a state from any other version, and the step reads `moveset.commands.special1/2` (step.ts:392-393). The obvious quick design adds `DuelConfig.kits` outside the moveset. The version would then no longer cover everything the step reads, so a state could be stepped, restored or replayed with different kits and nothing would refuse it. Settle it before starting: put all kit data in the `DuelMoveset` (kit moves in `moves`, plus a `kits` record of special1/special2 per kit), so the version covers it. Keep `moveset.commands` as the Duelist's, because DuelRoom.ts:315 reads `commands.throw`. Store each fighter's kit id in `FighterState` so that it is hashed, snapshotted and checked by `restoreDuel`, and set it with `createDuelState(config, { seed, kits })`. `DuelConfig`, `DuelAuthority` and `DuelClientSession` then stay unchanged, and the kits travel in snapshots.
concerns.consequence: If kits sit in the config outside the version, a server and client with different kit assignments run the same versioned state without any refusal. They drift apart and resync on every hash check instead of failing loudly. `fruit-kits-online` would also have to send the kits through the server, web and protocol layers into every `DuelConfig`, and would probably have to rework this feature's state shape.

concerns.message: Code outside the owned paths compiles against the content move types. apps/web/src/arenaScene.ts:58-62 calls `findMove(moveset, id)` and passes `move.hitbox` to `worldBox` as a required `Box`. It also uses `moveset.fighter.hurtboxes[stance]` (line 144) and `moveset.arena`. DuelRoom.ts:315 reads `config.moveset.commands.throw`. The natural way to model non-striking specials (feint dash, smoke screen) is a discriminated union without a hitbox, or an optional `hitbox`. Either one breaks typecheck in apps/web.
concerns.consequence: `npm run typecheck` fails in a path the worker doesn't own. That triggers the 'only by changing a path outside' stop, or a late rework of the schema. Keep `hitbox: Box` required on every `DuelMove`, and mark non-striking moves with a flag or optional sub-objects (`projectile?`, `zone?`, `cancel?`) instead.

concerns.message: The step assumes each fighter can make at most one contact per frame. It holds one `Contact` per attacker (step.ts:71) and has three rules built on melee range. On a hit near a wall, the leftover pushback moves the attacker back (step.ts:103). Guard direction comes from the attacker's position (step.ts:242). A strike landing on the same frame beats a grab (step.ts:80-84). A bolt adds a second source of contact per fighter. The plan doesn't say what happens when a melee hit and a bolt land on the same frame, whether a bolt stops a grab, which way to hold to block a bolt when the attacker has been crossed over, whether the attacker's `strikeInvulnerable` covers a bolt, or what two bolts do when they meet.
concerns.consequence: Without explicit rules, outcomes can depend on processing order, which breaks the 'neither fighter first' property. Bolts can become unblockable in cross-ups, breaking §9's 'no unavoidable damage'. An Ember at full screen can be shoved by wall pushback from its own bolt. Each of these is only found by the 1,800-frame property test, late in the run.

concerns.message: The whiffed-bolt punish test conflicts with §8's projectile row. duelist.ts takes baseline timings with `baseline(id)`, and `sameTiming` (schema.ts:216) locks any move whose id matches a baseline row. A bolt with exactly 22 startup and 30 recovery lasts 52 frames. A Duelist who jumps it on reaction is airborne for 40 frames and then needs 18 frames of heavy startup, so it can't punish. The bolt also can't be `high`, because any crouch dodges highs (step.ts:237), so crouching would beat it at every range. It needs to be a `mid`.
concerns.consequence: The worker either writes a contrived test (a point-blank bolt that spawns past the defender) that proves nothing about 'long recovery if attacks miss', or spends time fighting the budget check. Recommend: the bolt gets its own id; §8's 22/30 are floors, with the exception written in the data; the whiff test is a Duelist forward-jumping over the bolt from mid range and then landing a heavy.

concerns.message: Two acceptance terms have no meaning in the current schema. 'A special without a hurtbox is refused': moves have no hurtbox, only `stance` selecting `fighter.hurtboxes`. 'Within §8's budgets': §8 only has a row for the projectile. The flare, feint and screen have no row. The schema also rejects non-strike specials outright: `damage` and `hitstun` must be positive, strikes must match the blockstun formula, the start-gap reach check covers every move's hitbox (schema.ts:256) and does not know about projectile travel, and `duelMoveTimingSchema` rejects `projectile-life`.
concerns.consequence: The worker invents the meanings, and the budget and hurtbox tests may prove nothing. Worse, a per-move hurtbox used in `detect` for Duelist moves would quietly change the Duelist mirror. Recommend: `hurtbox` is required for specials and must equal the stance hurtbox on existing Duelist moves. 'Within budget' is written down in docs/fruit-kits.md as named checks: startup at or above the §8 minimum, recovery at or above 30, and on-block advantage consistent with blockstun.

concerns.message: There is no cancel system today. `canAct` requires `timer === 0`, and the only mid-move switch is `chordThrow`. The feint 'cancellable into a normal' adds one. If the feint can cancel into itself or into a special, or its `strikeInvulnerable` restarts on each cancel, chained feints give intangibility with no end. Bolts have a related loop risk: a bolt dies on hit, so a new one can be fired at once, and if bolt hitstun exceeds the next bolt's startup plus travel, full-screen bolts combo until the cap.
concerns.consequence: Both break §9's 'no permanent intangibility' and 'no automatic stun loops'. Neither has an acceptance test. The random property test is unlikely to find them because random inputs rarely produce frame-perfect chains. Add scripted tests: feint→feint and feint→special are refused, and a second bolt fired as early as possible after a bolt hit can be blocked.

concerns.message: 'Byte-for-byte today's Duelist mirror' can't hold literally. `movesetVersion` changes by design, and new state fields (kit ids, projectiles, screen) change `hashState` for every duel. No test outside the owned paths pins a hash; the only pinned value is `MOVESET_VERSION` in determinism.test.ts:137, which is owned. So nothing actually proves the kit-less duel still behaves the same. Existing scripted tests cover only specific scenarios.
concerns.consequence: A step refactor for projectiles or cancels could change Duelist behaviour (pushback, separation, buffer order) and still pass every existing test. That would silently change the netcode's and rooms' combat.

concerns.message: The property tests cover only the three mixed pairs. Mirrors are left out: Ember vs Ember (two bolts, bolt-vs-bolt contact) and Smoke vs Smoke (two screens overlapping, a fighter inside the opponent's screen). The plan also doesn't bound how many screens can exist at once, and `restoreDuel` needs a length bound on that list.
concerns.consequence: The mirror cases, which exercise the new entity code the most, go untested. `restoreDuel` validation may accept any list length, or refuse a legal state, once `fruit-kits-online` allows mirrors.

simpler_alternative: Make the kits pure data plus two small add-ons to the step. Keep `DuelConfig` and `DuelMove`'s shape (hitbox stays required). Put all moves in one `moves` list, add `kits: { duelist, ember, smoke }` holding each kit's special1/special2 ids, and keep `commands` as the Duelist's. Store `kit` per fighter in `FighterState` and read that fighter's special commands from `moveset.kits[fighter.kit]`. Model the flare as an ordinary strike with strike invulnerability during startup (like counter-slash), and the feint as an attack-action move whose `advance` and `strikeInvulnerable` ≤ startup give the dash plus a ≥N-frame reappearance recovery. Only the bolt and the screen need new state: `projectiles` (at most one per fighter) and `zones` (at most one per fighter). Each gets one resolution function that turns bolt overlaps into the same `Contact` the step already uses, with melee taking priority on one defender per frame. This leaves out FighterAction values and a general entity system, which would break the renderer's switches.
cheap_experiment: Before editing any code, at the base commit, run a seeded random-input Duelist-vs-Duelist duel over 1,800 frames (the determinism test's generator), plus the existing scripted scenarios. Record the canonical JSON of every frame's `fighters`, `events`, `phase` and `result` (not `movesetVersion`) as a fixture beside the new tests. After the kit changes, run the same inputs with no kits and compare the same fields. About 20 minutes of work. It proves that a kit-less duel is the same duel apart from the version and the new fields, and it catches any Duelist drift from the step refactor on the first run. If it fails early, that argues for bolting the entities on beside the step rather than threading them through it.
